content.title: About
content.content: Canned clams are a seafood product made from fresh clams that are cleaned, cooked, and sealed in an airtight jar with brine or sauce. They retain a delicate marine flavor, a faint sweetness, and a tender yet firm texture. The product is ready to eat straight from the can.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Clams are bivalve mollusks and have been harvested by humans for thousands of years.
Canning extends the shelf life of clams up to three years while preserving most of their nutrients.
Canned clams are sold in brine, oil, or tomato sauce, each giving a distinct taste profile.
Clams are rich in iron, zinc, and vitamin B12, making them a valuable addition for pescatarians.
In many cultures clams are considered a delicacy and are served as appetizers with sparkling wine.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Canned clams provide about 12 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Rich in minerals
items.content: They contain notable amounts of iron, zinc, and selenium, essential for immune function and metabolism.

items.title: Vitamin B12 source
items.content: Vitamin B12 is crucial for nervous system health and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Canned clams typically have less than 2 g of fat per 100 g, suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: They provide EPA and DHA, which support heart and brain health.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to clams.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Canned clams often contain a lot of salt; people with hypertension should limit intake.

items.title: Possible toxins
items.content: If harvested from polluted waters, clams may contain heavy metals or biotoxins.

items.title: Bacterial growth after opening
items.content: Once opened, store the clams in the refrigerator and consume within 1–2 days.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned clams can be eaten straight from the jar, added to salads, pasta, rice dishes, or soups. They are also used in stuffing for pies and as a topping for toast. For extra flavor, briefly sauté clams with garlic and herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, transfer clams to an airtight container and refrigerate, using them within 2 days.
